Tokyo

Wed Nov 11 – Sat Nov 14 · 3 nights

Stay: Hotel Sunroute Plaza Shinjuku, 3 nights — Shinjuku Station south exit. Narita Express runs direct to Shinjuku; Udon Shin and Fuunji are minutes away on foot; the Shibuya sumo session and Meiji Shrine are a short hop away; Yoyogi Park is at the doorstep for a backup run. Checkout Saturday morning — big bags takkyubin to Kyoto, the Fuji-day car carries the overnight bags to Hakone.

Arrival day — land at Narita, train in, keep it easy. Times assume an afternoon landing; slide everything with your flight.

~2:00 PM🚄 Land NRT — Welcome Suica, Narita Express direct to Shinjuku (~80 min)
4:30 PM🚄 Check in at Sunroute Plaza — south exit, no transfer
5:00 PM🎟️ Walk the neighborhood — Southern Terrace, the backstreets, feel the vibes of home base
5:45 PM⛩️ Shinjuku by neon — Omoide Yokocho’s lantern alleys (walk them, eat elsewhere), Kabukicho, the Godzilla head
7:00 PM🍜 Udon Shin — carbonara udon + a classic bowl, 5-min walk from the hotel
8:30 PM🍜 Bar Coo, Golden Gai — cash nightcap, a 15-min walk through Kabukicho; skip if the flight won
10:00 PM🍜 Swing by 7-Eleven — egg sando, onigiri, one mystery dessert — then sleep; dawn start tomorrow

Meals

Udon ShinShinjuku’s famous handmade udon, 5 minutes from the hotel — split the carbonara udon and a classic bowl. Ticket queue moves fast. (Fuunji tsukemen, also steps away, is the backup if the line is wild.)
7-Eleven run late snackThe inaugural konbini stop — egg sando, onigiri, one mystery dessert. A trip tradition starts tonight.
Bar Coo barThe tiny Golden Gai nightcap — cash, after 8pm, walkable from the hotel. Unbookable, so zero arrival-night risk; push it to another night if jet lag wins.

Experiences

Settle in + neighborhood lapWelcome Suica at the airport, drop bags — then a slow walk of the blocks around the hotel to feel the vibes before dinner.

Sightseeing

Shinjuku by neonOmoide Yokocho’s lantern alleys (walk-through — eat elsewhere), Kabukicho, the Godzilla head. Learn your home turf on night one.
Bonuses — only if time allows
  • Fuunji — the backup tsukemen bowl, also steps from the hotel
  • Don Quijote, Kabukicho — the chaotic late-night megastore run; Kit-Kat flavors + anything you forgot to pack
  • Yoyogi Park twilight stroll — at your doorstep, good for shaking off the flight
  • Shibuya Crossing — one Yamanote stop away, if you want the full neon baptism tonight instead of Friday

Dawn run, old Tokyo, the west-side loop — then the Shinjuku izakaya tour (booked ✓) to finish. The fullest day of the trip; cut Koenji if dragging.

6:00 AM🎟️ Imperial Palace 5K — Chuo line, 15 min from Shinjuku (Yoyogi Park at the doorstep is the lazy fallback)
8:00 AM⛩️ Senso-ji before the tour buses, breakfast nearby, then wander the Asakusa backstreets
12:15 PM🎟️ Nakano Broadway — shops open around now
1:45 PM🎟️ Koenji vintage racks, one stop over
2:30 PM🍜 ISENTEI late pizza lunch, Inokashira Park stroll
3:45 PM🎟️ Shimokitazawa — vintage racks + a quick Oribe coffee; leave by 4:40, Odakyu straight to Shinjuku
5:00 PM🎟️ Shinjuku Izakaya Tour with an Expert — booked ✓ (2 guests, $200.10); izakaya school on home turf, dinner handled
~8:00 PM🍜 Tour ends in Shinjuku — stroll home, or Golden Gai round two

Meals

ISENTEI lunchPizzeria inside Inokashira Park — a 200-year-old teahouse, Naples world-championship medalist at the oven.
Shinjuku Izakaya Tour with an Expert booked ✓5:00 PM, 2 guests, $200.10 paid. Izakaya school on home turf — message the guide ahead that you want the ordering playbook taught, not just shown; you’ll run it solo in Kyoto and Osaka. Dinner is the tour.

Experiences

Imperial Palace run5K at dawn, counterclockwise. Runner stations rent lockers and showers.
Koenji + Nakano Broadway shoppingVintage racks, then the otaku collectibles labyrinth one Chuo stop away. Broadway shops open ~noon.
Shimokitazawa vintage shoppingTokyo’s best secondhand maze — work the racks around the station before Oribe.
Oribe cafe + shopShimokitazawa kissaten doubling as a Mino-ware ceramics shop — today it’s a quick coffee and a scan of the shelves; the Odakyu runs straight to Shinjuku for the 5pm tour.

Sightseeing

Senso-ji, AsakusaRight after the run, before the tour buses.
Inokashira ParkPost-lunch stroll — ponds, swan boats, momiji starting.
Bonuses — only if time allows
  • Lad’s Dining — the pizza dinner, if lunch pizza didn’t cover it
  • Swan boat on Inokashira pond — twenty silly minutes after ISENTEI
  • Golden Gai round two — the tour ends on home turf; the alley is a short walk if you still have gas
  • Shirube, Shimokitazawa — Mustafa’s dinner pick: the beloved izakaya with the blowtorched mackerel finished at your table. Tonight’s dinner is the booked tour, but if plans shift — or you fall for Shimokita and come back — this is the move
  • Kintsugi at mon cadeau — gold-repair workshop on Dogenzaka, Shibuya (2 hrs, ~¥20k, matcha + sweets included; book ahead). Thursday is already full — it fits Friday better if you want it
Izakaya playbook — learn it tonight, use it all trip
  • “Toriaezu, nama de” — “draft beer to start”; the universal opener while you think
  • Otoshi — the small dish that appears unasked; it’s a seating charge, not a mistake
  • “Osusume wa?” — “what do you recommend?” — the best menu in any room
  • “Sumimasen!” — call the staff; nobody comes until you do, and that’s polite
  • “Kore o kudasai” + pointing — fully legitimate ordering; menus and neighbors’ plates are fair game
  • “Okaikei onegaishimasu” — the check; pay at the register, never tip

Sumo in the morning, ginkgo gold — Shibuya Sky at sunset only if you feel like it.

11:45 AM⛩️ Meiji Shrine through the forest gate — one Yamanote stop north

4:15 PM⛩️ Optional: Shibuya Sky at sunset (~4:40, needs advance booking) — or just wander Ginza and drift toward Shibuya at your own pace
6:30 PM🍜 Tacos 3Hermanos, Harajuku
8:30 PM🍜 Mikkeller Tokyo, Shibuya

Step Into the World of Sumo booked · 9:30amHands-on morning session in Shibuya, booked via Airbnb for 2 ($126.84 paid). From there it’s one Yamanote stop up to Meiji Shrine.

Meiji ShrineForest approach, morning quiet.
Jingu Gaien ginkgo avenueThe one city foliage that peaks near these dates.
Bonuses — only if time allows

The Romancecar booked ✓Odakyu’s limited express from Shinjuku — tickets in hand; just be on the platform ten minutes early with the overnight bags.

Hakone + Kamakura

Sat Nov 14 – Mon Nov 16 · 2 nights

Stay: Hotel Morinokaze Hakone Sengokuhara, 2 nights — onsen resort in the Sengokuhara highlands, ~30 min by Hakone Tozan bus from Hakone-Yumoto, next to the famous silver pampas-grass fields. Tattoos: reserve the private (kashikiri) bath slots — communal baths generally bar them.

The full Hakone circuit — sculptures, volcano, lake — ending in the bath.

7:30 AM🎟️ Morning soak + breakfast at the hotel
9:00 AM🚄 Bus from Sengokuhara toward Gora
9:30 AM⛩️ Hakone Open-Air Museum — 2 hrs among the sculptures
12:00 PM🍜 Lunch in Gora, then the Tozan cable car up to Sounzan
1:00 PM🎟️ Ropeway over Owakudani — black eggs at the crater stop
2:30 PM🎟️ Ropeway down to Togendai — pirate ship across Lake Ashi
3:30 PM⛩️ Hakone Shrine — the torii standing in the water
4:45 PM🚄 Bus back toward Sengokuhara
5:30 PM⛩️ Susuki pampas-grass fields at golden hour — steps from the hotel, November peak
6:30 PM🍜 Dinner at the hotel, long soak after

Meals

Owakudani black eggs snackBoiled in the volcanic springs — each one supposedly buys you seven more years.

Experiences

The Hakone loopMuseum → cable car → ropeway → pirate ship — the transit is the attraction. A Hakone Freepass covers it all.
Onsen, twiceMorning and night — book the kashikiri private bath if tattoos apply.

Sightseeing

Hakone Open-Air MuseumSculpture park in the hills — Picasso pavilion, foot bath, fall color between the works.

Bonuses — only if time allows

  • Old cedar avenue, Moto-Hakone — a short stretch of the Edo-era highway by the lake

Meals

Lunch in ArashiyamaYudofu (simmered tofu) is the local specialty; riverside spots near Togetsukyo.

Experiences

Hozugawa river boat not bookedKameoka → Arashiyama: 16 km of gorge, ~2 hrs, aiming for the noon departure. Reserve online the day before; go/no-go decided day-of on river conditions — if it cancels, the Sagano Romantic Train is the fallback.
Iwatayama Monkey Park optionalA genuine 20-minute uphill, monkeys, the best free view over Kyoto — but it’s first on today’s cut list. Gate before 4pm or not at all.

Sightseeing

Arashiyama riverside + TogetsukyoWhere the boat lands — the gorge in full color.
Bamboo grove, 8amNow the must-do opener — in its quiet hour it’s the postcard; by 10 it’s a corridor of phones.
Bonuses — only if time allows
  • %Arabica, riverside — the famous little coffee counter facing Togetsukyo
  • Sagano Romantic Train back — ride the scenic rail up the same gorge you floated down
  • Saga Toriimoto + Otagi Nenbutsu-ji — keep walking north past the crowds: a preserved street ending at 1,200 moss-covered rakan statues, each with a different face. The quiet Arashiyama almost nobody reaches
  • Kimono Forest — the lit kimono-fabric pillars at Randen Arashiyama station; free, two minutes, on the way

Kaiseki dinner still to bookThe splurge meal — book now and ask for a late ~8pm seating so Eikando fits first; take an earlier slot only if 8 isn’t offered.

Daimonji hikeThe midday gap, used properly: trailhead by Ginkaku-ji, ~45 minutes up to the giant 大 fire-bed with the whole city below. Real shoes, down well before dark.

Sightseeing

Kiyomizu-deraGates open 6am; tour groups roll in around 8 — at your start you’ll be walking down Sannenzaka as they arrive, which is the whole trick.

  • Nijo Castle — the shogun’s nightingale-floor palace; the free block’s best structured option. Do it first, then eat and shop your way back. (And skip Nishiki Market — locals now call it a tourist trap; only duck in if you’re literally passing)
  • Kamo River run — the free-block option; flat, riverside, straight from the hotel
  • Gion Shirakawa at dusk — if you missed it Monday night
  • Anything skipped earlier — Kennin-ji, the sake district, or the Nintendo store all fit this afternoon

Thirteen days in Japan

The whole trip as one story, told day by day — what each morning is for, where the night ends, and the one thing not to miss. Illustrations in the style of the map; the tabs above hold the full timings.

Wednesday, Nov 11 — Land, and learn your corner of Shinjuku

Tokyo · night 1 of 3 at Sunroute Plaza

The flight lands mid-afternoon and the only job is arrival done well: NEX straight to Shinjuku, bags down, then a slow lap of Southern Terrace to feel the vibes of home base. After dark it's the neon orientation — Omoide Yokocho's lanterns (walked, not eaten), Kabukicho, the Godzilla head — then handmade udon at Udon Shin, a cash nightcap at tiny Bar Coo in Golden Gai if the flight didn't win, and the first 7-Eleven run of the trip. A tradition begins.

Photo: IQRemix from Canada · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

Thursday, Nov 12 — Old Tokyo, the west side, and izakaya school

Tokyo · the fullest day · izakaya tour booked ✓

A dawn 5K around the Imperial Palace moat, Senso-ji before the crowds, then a slow wander through Asakusa's backstreets. The afternoon rides the Chuo line west — Nakano Broadway's collector maze, Koenji's racks, championship pizza inside Inokashira Park, a fast pass through Shimokitazawa. At five, the booked Shinjuku Izakaya Tour: three hours of ordering school on home turf, so every dinner for the next eleven days gets easier. Cut Koenji if you're dragging — the night matters more.

Photo: Dick Thomas Johnson from Tokyo, Japan · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

Friday, Nov 13 — Sumo hands-on, shrine forest, golden gingko

Tokyo · sumo experience booked ✓

The booked morning: Step Into the World of Sumo in Shibuya — ninety minutes with retired rikishi, since November's real tournament is away in Fukuoka. Then the Meiji forest, Harajuku's La Forêt and PAP, and the gingko avenue at Jingu Gaien right as it turns. A katsu sando from the Ginza shop that invented it, tacos at 3Hermanos, Mikkeller to close. Shibuya Sky stays optional; the kintsugi studio on Dogenzaka fits the 4:15 gap if you want gold in your hands.

Photo: Moyan Brenn from Italy · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

Saturday, Nov 14 — the Romancecar south, then the first onsen

Tokyo → Hakone · Romancecar booked ✓ · night 1 of 2 at Morinokaze

The first slow morning of the trip, then downstairs to the Odakyu platforms and onto the Romancecar — eighty-five minutes of windows to Hakone-Yumoto. Lunch on the river street, the Tozan bus up to Sengokuhara, and by three you’re at Morinokaze with the susuki pampas fields next door catching the late light. Then the first private kashikiri bath of the trip — reserved for the two of you, tattoos welcome by design. Hotel dinner. Fuji herself waits for tomorrow’s ropeway, skies permitting.

Photo: Guilhem Vellut from Annecy, France · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

Sunday, Nov 15 — The whole Hakone circuit

Hakone · night 2 · Hakone Freepass day

The classic loop, run clockwise: the Open-Air Museum at opening, lunch in Gora, the Tozan cable car and ropeway over Owakudani's steaming valley — black eggs obligatory — then the pirate ship across Lake Ashi to the shrine with the torii standing in the water. Back for golden hour in the susuki fields, a second kashikiri soak, dinner at the hotel. The one day of the trip with no decisions in it: the mountain runs the show.

Photo: Jean-Pierre Dalbéra from Paris, France · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

Monday, Nov 16 — The Buddha on the way to the lanterns

Hakone → Kamakura → Kyoto · night 1 of 5 in Gion · day rank #5

Check out, drop down to Odawara, and take the forty-minute detour history deserves: the Great Buddha at Kotoku-in, Hokokuji's bamboo with matcha in the garden, shirasu-don by the station. The shinkansen runs you west by late afternoon, and Kyoto opens at night: the must-do first walk down lantern-lit Hanamikoji, Kodai-ji's autumn light-up if there's energy, and a Pontocho counter where Thursday's izakaya playbook gets its first solo run.

Photo: Basile Morin · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

Tuesday, Nov 17 — Ten thousand torii at first light

Kyoto · day rank #2 · Nandattei reserved ✓

On the first Keihan train south, into the gates at 6:15 — the foliage-first call: climb to the Yotsutsuji overlook, watch Kyoto wake up, and turn back rather than looping the summit. That trade buys Tofuku-ji at its 8:30 opening bell, the best maple valley in the city before the buses find it. The afternoon is deliberately soft — an optional Kamo River jog or nothing at all — then reserved ramen at Nandattei. Karaoke sits on the bench unless the night insists.

Photo: Basile Morin · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

Wednesday, Nov 18 — Bamboo at dawn, then down the gorge

Kyoto · day rank #3 · noon boat NOT booked yet

Arashiyama runs on last-entry times, so the order is everything: the bamboo grove at 7:45 in its one quiet hour, Okochi Sanso's garden if the morning allows, then the JR to Kameoka to make the pier by 11:30. The noon Hozugawa boat — two hours of gorge in full color, still unbooked, decided day-of by the river — lands you at Togetsukyo for a late yudofu lunch. The Monkey Park is first on the cut list: gate before four or let it go gracefully.

Photo: Immanuel Giel · CC0 · Wikimedia Commons

Thursday, Nov 19 — Bowing deer and the Great Buddha

Nara day trip · day rank #4

An early train south to the oldest capital: senbei crackers and politely mobbing deer in the park, the Great Buddha filling Todai-ji's enormous hall, warm mochi from Nakatanidou's high-speed pounders at noon. The afternoon walk is Kasuga Taisha's forest approach, lined with thousands of stone lanterns — unlit by day, lovely anyway. If legs agree, Byodo-in at Uji is one stop on the line home: the temple on the ten-yen coin. Then an easy Gion evening, because tomorrow starts at six.

Photo: Martin Falbisoner · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

Friday, Nov 20 — The #1 day: temple stage, mountain fire-bed, lit maples

Kyoto · day rank #1 · kaiseki still to book (ask ~8pm)

Kiyomizu-dera at its six o'clock opening, the great wooden stage floating over red maples with the lanes to yourselves — you'll walk down Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka just as the tour groups walk up. Bags ship to Osaka mid-morning, and the midday gap goes to the Daimonji hike: forty-five minutes above Ginkaku-ji to the giant 大 fire-bed, the whole city below, down well before dark. At 5:30, Eikando's illumination — the one night of your stay it runs — then the kaiseki splurge at a late seating. The best day, start to finish.

Photo: DXR · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

Saturday, Nov 21 — A waterfall hike, then the neon canal

Kyoto → Minoh → Osaka · night 1 of 2 in Namba · ★ Bar Nyuta

Leave temple Japan in the morning and climb into maple Japan: the Minoh Falls trail outside Osaka, with momiji tempura — fried maple leaves — sold along the path. By late afternoon you're checked into Namba, and the volume goes up: the Dotonbori neon reflected in the canal, negiyaki at Fukutaro, and the starred must of the whole Osaka leg — cocktails at Bar Nyuta. Run the izakaya playbook anywhere that glows.

Photo: Martin Falbisoner · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

Sunday, Nov 22 — Castle moat at dawn, theme park all day

Osaka · USJ · Express Pass still URGENT to book

A 6:30 run around the Osaka Castle moat while the city sleeps in, then the one day engineered in advance: Universal Studios on a holiday Sunday. The Express Pass with timed Nintendo-area entry is the whole ballgame — it's the last unbooked lynchpin of the trip — and Kinopio's Cafe gets queued in the app the moment you're through the gates. Stay until the lights come on; Namba's late-night kitchens will still be open when you crawl home.

Photo: 国土地理院 · Attribution · Wikimedia Commons

Monday, Nov 23 — Pork buns, then the long hop home

Osaka → KIX → Narita → LAX · Labor Thanksgiving Day

One last 551 Horai pork bun, the Nankai line to Kansai airport, and the trip's only nervous math: Peach to Narita with a four-hour buffer before the ZIPAIR leg, protected on separate tickets by arriving absurdly early on a holiday Monday. Then the Pacific, and a camera roll that starts with Shinjuku neon and ends with a sunrise over the sea. Thirteen days, four cities, two onsens, one gold-repaired bowl if Friday went that way.

Ten phrases

tap 🔊 to hear each one spoken

Audio uses your device's Japanese voice — on iPhone it may take one tap to warm up. Speak slowly, bow slightly, and sumimasen covers the rest.

こんにちは

Konnichiwa

Hello / good afternoon

The all-day greeting — mornings it's ohayō gozaimasu, evenings konbanwa.

Photo: senngokujidai4434 · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

ありがとうございます

Arigatō gozaimasu

Thank you (polite)

Say it to every clerk and server; a small nod comes free.

Photo: Mr.ちゅらさん · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

すみません

Sumimasen

Excuse me / sorry / hey!

The most useful word in Japan — call izakaya staff with it, apologize with it, squeeze past crowds with it.

Photo: m-louis .® · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

お願いします

Onegaishimasu

Please / I'll have that

Hand over a ramen ticket or confirm any request with this.

Photo: Nikos Roussos from Athens, Greece · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

これをください

Kore o kudasai

This one, please

Point at the plastic food models or a menu line — solves 90% of ordering.

Photo: Real Estate Japan from Tokyo, Japan · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

いくらですか？

Ikura desu ka?

How much is it?

For market stalls like Kuromon — the answer comes fast, so watch the register display.

Photo: Choi2451 · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

トイレはどこですか？

Toire wa doko desu ka?

Where is the toilet?

Also look for お手洗い (o-tearai) on signs.

Photo: Mattias Hallberg · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

英語を話せますか？

Eigo o hanasemasu ka?

Do you speak English?

Station and JR info counters almost always do.

Photo: 掬茶 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

おいしい！

Oishii!

Delicious!

Say it mid-bite and watch the chef light up.

Photo: Joli Rumi · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

乾杯！

Kanpai!

Cheers!

Wait until everyone's drink lands, then all together — made for Thursday's izakaya tour.

Photo: Benreis · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
